title: Maximum Number of Distinct Elements After Operations
statement: Each element of `nums` may be shifted at most once: you add to it some integer from `-k` to `k` (inclusive), and different elements may use different amounts. After the shifts, count how many distinct values the array holds. Return the largest count you can achieve.
notes:
## Intuition

Each element can land anywhere in its window `[num - k, num + k]`, and we want as many elements as possible on different integers. Go through the elements from smallest to largest and give each one the smallest integer in its window that is above every integer used so far. Taking the smallest possible value leaves the most room for the larger elements still to come, and because all windows have the same width, a later window never ends before an earlier one. If even that smallest value lies past the window's end, the element can only repeat a used value, so it adds nothing. (Trying every combination of shifts also works, but takes (2k + 1)^n time.)

## Approach

1. Sort `nums`.
2. `last` is the largest value used so far, starting at minus infinity, and `distinct` counts the values used.
3. For each `num`, the best `value` is `max(last + 1, num - k)`.
4. If `value <= num + k`, use it: increase `distinct` and set `last = value`. Otherwise skip the element; it will repeat a value.
5. Return `distinct`.

## Example 1, step by step

Sorted `nums` is `[1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4]` with `k = 2`. The first `1` takes `-1`, the bottom of its window `[-1, 3]`. Then `2` takes `0`, the next `2` takes `1`, the two `3`s take `2` and `3`, and `4` takes `4`, each inside its window. All six elements fit, so the answer is `6`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n) for the sort; the scan is O(n).
- Space: O(1) besides the sort.

## Pitfalls

- Start `last` below every reachable value: shifted values can be negative, so 0 is not low enough.
- When an element does not fit, skip it and keep going; a later, larger element may still fit.
- Without sorting, an element can take a value that a smaller element needed.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `num` | the current element, in sorted order |
| `value` | the smallest unused integer its window allows |
| `last` | the largest value used so far |
| `distinct` | how many different values have been used |

narration.2: Sort so the elements, and their equal-width windows, come from left to right.
narration.3: No distinct values have been placed yet.
narration.4: The largest value used so far; minus infinity means nothing is used yet.
narration.5: Handle the elements from smallest to largest.
narration.6: The smallest integer that is inside this window and above every value used so far.
narration.7: Is that integer still inside the window [num - k, num + k]?
narration.8: Yes: this element gets a value of its own.
narration.9: Remember it as the largest value used.
narration.12: Every element that found room counts once.
